messages:
lauren: proposing a new 'pulsed holdpoint' staircase rollout for model upgrades — idea is small quick pulses with explicit holdpoints and an automated telemetry gate before each bump. want feedback on percent steps and guard thresholds.
ben: curious, how is this different from our current staggered ramp?
mike: +1 to holdpoints. current ramps are too smooth; we often miss regressions that show up only after a short spike. pulses would make regressions surface faster.
claire: UX question: how will this appear in the console? users need a simple mental model. maybe show the pulse schedule and next hold expiry with a clear PASS/FAIL gate state.
lauren: rough schedule I'm thinking: [1% -> hold 10m], [5% -> hold 15m], [20% -> hold 30m], [50% -> hold 60m], [100%]. Each hold checks: error-rate < 0.5% relative increase, p95 latency delta < +100ms, and quality metrics (eval set) within tolerance.
olivia: for noisy workloads, those hold durations might be too short. suggest min samples check, e.g., require at least 200 requests during hold or extend hold with rolling window.
lauren: good point. add quota-aware sample gating: if samples < threshold, auto-extend by 2x up to a ceiling. also add forced rollback if certain hard-fails hit.
ben: can we express this as a compact config? want an API shape the console and rollout engine can both interpret.
mike: here's a proto config sketch:
```
rollout:
  mode: pulsed
  steps:
    - percent: 1
      hold_mins: 10
      min_samples: 200
      gates:
        - type: telemetry_delta
          metric: error_rate
          allowed_relative_increase: 0.005
        - type: telemetry_delta
          metric: p95_latency_ms
          allowed_absolute_increase: 100
    - percent: 5
      hold_mins: 15
      min_samples: 500
    - percent: 20
      hold_mins: 30
    - percent: 50
      hold_mins: 60
    - percent: 100
      hold_mins: 0
  backoff_policy: quota_aware
  max_auto_extend_mins: 120
```
ben: love the proto. question: how do we handle cohorts and sticky routing? we'll need deterministic split keys so experiments aren't jittery.
claire: console should show cohort buckets and a preview of which requests map to canary vs control for a given keyspace (example: user_id % 100 < N).
olivia: telemetry-bot, can we add a gate type for 'quality jitter' — compare semantic eval score distributions and flag if KL divergence > threshold?
telemetry-bot: yes, we can compute distribution divergence during hold window and emit PASS/FAIL. suggesting KL threshold 0.02 to start. will need eval dataset mapping.
mike: also recommend a safety hold if region capacity is constrained — i.e., if dedicated pool CPU/GPU usage > 85% then pause and alert.
lauren: agree. add infra_capacity gate. if infra fails, rollout pauses and route falls back to previous model variant. we should add explicit fallback policy in config.
ben: policy question: auto-approve to next step vs manual confirmation. I'd prefer auto with strict gates for dev/test, manual for customer-tiered Dedicated. add a policy flag 'approval: auto|manual|hybrid'.
lauren: yep. default auto for internal and dev, hybrid for prod where last step requires manual sign-off.
mike: logging/telemetry hooks: for every hold window, emit a compact snapshot: {step, percent, samples, error_rate_delta, latency_delta, kl_score, infra_headroom}. console shows green/yellow/red for each.
claire: UX: add a single-click 'abort and rollback' that triggers immediate 0% routing and marks rollout as aborted with reason. keep history of snapshots for postmortem.
lauren: thanks — i'll draft a PR for the rollout-engine with the proto and a console mock. will include unit tests for gate evaluation and a simulation harness to run fuzzy tests against noisy workloads.
ben: please include canary analytics: time-to-detect and false-positive rate from simulation, so we can tune thresholds.
lauren: noted.
deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: id=r-2026-04-03-09 pulsed mode, start_ts=2176543210, initial_step=1%
mike: also add a footgun protection: require owners to opt-in for any rollout that touches >30% in first 24h for Dedicated customers.
olivia: agreed. security/ops also wants a checklist: KMS usage for model artifacts, audit log enabled for every step.
lauren: will add checklist items. thanks all — i'll drop the PR link when ready. :rocket:
